categories.main_business_segments: Miura Co., Ltd. operates four main business segments: Domestic Equipment Sales (industrial and marine boilers, water treatment, medical, food processing, and laundry equipment), Domestic Maintenance (after-sales service, maintenance contracts, energy management), Overseas Equipment Sales (primarily boilers and related systems), and Overseas Maintenance (maintenance and service contracts for overseas customers). The company also engages in environmental analysis and engineering services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include compact once-through boiler design, advanced combustion and heat recovery systems, water treatment and purification technologies, IoT-based remote monitoring and maintenance, and automation for industrial and medical equipment. Production emphasizes energy efficiency, environmental compliance, and integration of digital solutions such as digital twins and IoT platforms for system optimization.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Miura serves a wide range of industrial customers, including manufacturing plants (food, chemicals, pharmaceuticals), hospitals and medical institutions, shipping and marine industries, commercial laundries, and public infrastructure. Its products are used in sectors requiring reliable steam, hot water, sterilization, and water treatment solutions.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates globally with a strong presence in Japan, Asia (notably China, South Korea, Taiwan, Southeast Asia), North America (especially the US and Canada), and expanding operations in Europe and South America. Recent acquisitions have significantly increased its footprint in the US and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: Miura is primarily positioned as a midstream and downstream supplier, manufacturing and assembling finished equipment and systems, and providing ongoing maintenance and service directly to end users and industrial operators.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding global market share, developing decarbonization and energy-saving solutions (such as hydrogen and ammonia boilers, high-efficiency fuel cells), enhancing IoT and digital service offerings, and providing total solutions for heat, water, and environmental needs. R&D focuses on sustainability, automation, and new energy sources, with active investment in M&A to acquire new technologies and market access.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through direct product sales (boilers, water treatment, medical and food processing equipment), long-term maintenance and service contracts, leasing, and energy management services. Maintenance and recurring service contracts are a significant and growing portion of revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key competitors include other global boiler and industrial equipment manufacturers such as Cleaver-Brooks (now a subsidiary), Fulton, and local/regional players in each market. Miura positions itself as a technology leader in compact, energy-efficient boilers and integrated maintenance services, with a strong reputation for reliability and environmental performance.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated revenue reached ¥251.3 billion, with operating profit of ¥25.3 billion and net profit attributable to owners of ¥23.3 billion. The company experienced rapid growth (57.4% YoY revenue increase), driven by acquisitions and overseas expansion, and aims for continued double-digit growth with a target of ¥300 billion in sales by FY2028.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Miura differentiates itself through highly efficient, environmentally friendly boiler systems, comprehensive maintenance and IoT-enabled service offerings, and the ability to deliver total solutions for heat, water, and environmental management. The company emphasizes sustainability, reliability, and lifecycle cost reduction, positioning itself as a long-term partner for industrial and institutional customers.
